speaker: Doctor
text: How long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and does the cough produce any phlegm or blood?

speaker: Patient
text: I've had this cough going on for over three weeks now. It's mostly dry, but sometimes I cough up a little white phlegm, and I've noticed I get quite short of breath when I try to walk or do any physical activity. However, the stroke team confirmed ischemic stroke before transfer. This session should only record the confirmed diagnosis, not re-assess.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is a critical detail; did the stroke occur before or after the cough began, and are you currently on any anticoagulant medications like warfarin or aspirin? REQUEST TEST: D-Dimer

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the normal D-Dimer result; that helps rule out a pulmonary embolism. Given your history of ischemic stroke and current shortness of breath, have you noticed any swelling in your legs or a change in your skin color? REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Right lower lobe consolidation consistent with a possible pneumonia. No pleural effusion noted.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Post-stroke pneumonia (Right lower lobe)
